items.title: AI is supercharging money scams – here’s what you can do to protect yourself
items.summary: For years, warnings about artificial intelligence and cybersecurity have focused on corporate networks and government systems. Those threats are real. But if you follow the money in the FBI’s fraud data, a different picture emerges: Staggering sums are flowing out of household accounts . In its 2025 annual report , the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center began tracking complaints with an AI connection for the first time. Americans filed more than 22,000 such cases and reported roughly US$893 million in losses. Investment fraud accounted for $632 million of that, and people over 60 accounted for $352 million of the losses. Those figures include only victims who reported to the FBI, and only cases where AI’s role could be identified. The consulting firm Deloitte projects that the actual hit from AI will be much bigger and help push U.S. fraud losses overall to $40 billion by 2027, up from $12.3 billion in 2023. I’m a finance professor who studies household finance and how people use AI to make money decisions . And I believe the most consequential AI security story right now isn’t unfolding in server rooms, but at kitchen tables. Old cons, new machinery None of these scams are new.

items.title: Nakkheeran journalist Prakash arrested for derogatory allegations against woman anchor
items.summary: The Chennai police on Wednesday, September 16, arrested journalist Damodaran Prakash, who works for Tamil investigative magazine Nakkheeran , for making derogatory remarks about a woman anchor who works with YouTuber Savukku Shankar. Prakash was arrested from his residence in Chintadripet, Chennai. According to the police, Prakash appeared in a video titled ‘HIV Savukku — Kalyanam’ which was published on YouTube in January this year, and made malicious rumours against the woman anchor saying that she had contracted HIV. The video, published on the YouTube channel King 24 X 7, featured the woman’s photograph and contained “false, disgusting statements regarding her personal life, thereby defaming womanhood,” police said. The case was registered at the S-8 Adambakkam Police Station based on a complaint filed by the woman. Police said Prakash was arrested under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Information Technology Act (IT Act) and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act (TNPHW Act).
